title: NY State Senate · District 35
area: Yonkers and other communities in southern/central Westchester County, including Greenburgh and Mount Pleasant.

context.text: Both major-party primaries for this seat were canceled; incumbent Andrea Stewart-Cousins advanced on the Democratic and Working Families lines and Anthony Merante advanced on the Republican line without appearing on a primary ballot.

candidates.name: Andrea Stewart-Cousins
candidates.currentRole: New York State Senate Majority Leader and President Pro Tempore, District 35 (senator since 2007, majority leader since January 2019)

summary.text: Andrea Stewart-Cousins is the Democratic and Working Families Party candidate for re-election to New York State Senate District 35. She has represented the district since 2007 and has served as Senate Majority Leader since January 2019, the first woman and first Black legislator to hold that position; as of January 2026 she was the longest-serving Democratic Senate majority leader in state history.

background.text: Earned a B.S. from Pace University and an M.P.A. from Pace University in 2008.
Worked as an English teacher, a journalist for Gannett, a human resources manager for Careerblazers, and a marketing professional for American Telephone & Telegraph before entering government.
Served as director of community affairs for the city of Yonkers from 1992 to 1996.
Represented District 16 on the Westchester County Board of Legislators from 1996 to 2006, serving as majority whip and later vice-chair; helped pass the county's 1999 Human Rights Law.
Served as acting Lieutenant Governor of New York for about two weeks in 2021, after Governor Andrew Cuomo's resignation and before Brian Benjamin was sworn in.
Elected Senate Democratic leader in December 2012 and became Senate Majority Leader in January 2019 after Democrats regained the chamber majority.

priorities.text: Lists education funding reform, voting reforms, and gun safety among her legislative priorities as Senate Majority Leader.
Lists reproductive rights protection, LGBTQ rights, and workplace harassment prevention among her legislative priorities.
Lists labor rights, tenant protections, and affordable housing initiatives among her legislative priorities.

"I appreciate the fact that people, over the years, have given me more and more responsibility, and I also believe that part of that is because I act responsibly with the power I get. So people trust me with more."

positions.summary: In a 2024 statement, welcomed Governor Hochul's signing of a package of gun-violence reduction laws, including measures on pistol converters and court-ordered firearm removal (ERPO) procedures.
positions.quote: As Majority Leader, I am proud of the bold, sensible steps New York continues to take to reduce gun violence and save lives. The signing of this critical package of gun violence reduction legislation, demonstrates New York's continued commitment to public safety.

record.text: Sponsored S10564, establishing a school speed-zone camera demonstration program in the city of Yonkers; signed by the Governor August 14, 2026 (Chapter 233).
Sponsored S8859, extending the city of Yonkers' authorization to issue bonds and notes through negotiated sales to June 30, 2027; signed by the Governor June 26, 2026 (Chapter 134).

Sponsored S10637-A, a concurrent resolution amending the state constitution's independent redistricting commission provisions; passed both houses and delivered to the Secretary of State June 17, 2026, pending voter approval at a general election.
Sponsored S10634, which would let the city of Yonkers impose a surcharge of up to triple the standard tax rate on vacant and abandoned property; remained in Senate Rules Committee as of June 1, 2026.
Re-elected Senate Majority Leader by the Democratic conference in December 2024, continuing as the chamber's presiding Democratic leader.

summary.text: Anthony Merante is a certified public accountant and former Yonkers City Councilmember (6th District, two terms) running for New York State Senate District 35 on the Republican line against Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins.

background.text: Holds a B.S. in Accounting from St. John's University (1982) and became a Certified Public Accountant in 1987.
Worked in accounting and tax services for small and mid-sized companies in the Yonkers and Westchester County region.
Served as president of the Sprain Lake Knolls Civic Association before being elected to the Yonkers City Council for the 6th District in 2017, completing two terms.

priorities.text: "Team Yonkers is united in fighting for better representation, lower taxes, safer streets, stronger schools, and real solutions that put Yonkers and Westchester families first."
"New Yorkers are being crushed by high taxes, soaring utility bills, unaffordable housing, rising insurance costs, and everyday expenses."
Describes himself as "a proven fighter for taxpayers" and says "government should work for the people, not special interests or political insiders."

positions.summary: Campaign site opposes state action to override local zoning to build housing projects.
positions.quote: Albany wants to override local zoning and build massive housing projects that would overcrowd and destroy neighborhoods. We must stop this Albany power grab.

researchNotes: Anthony Merante's Yonkers City Council record (2017–2025, two terms as 6th District Councilmember) was checked against yonkersny.legistar.com; reporting there documents him repeatedly casting the sole no vote on the city budget and a 6-1 vote on new council district maps, but no roll call was found on a bill squarely matching one of the guide's 15 fixed issue statements, so no vote-based record items or positions were added for him. Sen. Stewart-Cousins's federal-adjacent state floor votes above (S9500-A, S8455-B) were added per this guide's separate state-legislature vote process.
